title: YouTube / Video Streaming
subtitle: Designing a planet-scale video upload, DAG-based GOP chunk transcoding, and Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) HLS/DASH CDN delivery platform
keyTakeaways: Never upload or transcode a raw multi-gigabyte video as a single monolith: use S3 Multipart Presigned URLs for resumable chunked uploads and split the video at Group-of-Pictures (GOP / keyframe) boundaries so hundreds of worker containers transcode 4-second segments in parallel.

Deliver smooth playback over fluctuating mobile networks via Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) streaming (HLS `.m3u8` / MPEG-DASH `.mpd`): the client player measures real-time throughput and buffer health to dynamically switch between `360p`, `720p`, `1080p`, and `4K` fMP4 segments at every 4-second boundary.

Follow the 80/20 Pareto rule across multi-tier CDN storage: serve the top 5% viral videos directly from ISP Edge NVMe RAM/SSD caches (OpenConnect / Edge PoPs), the next 20% from Regional Origin Shields, and long-tail archival videos from S3 with Per-Title Convex-Hull encoding.

sections.heading: 1. Requirements Engineering & Scope Boundaries
sections.body: We are designing a global video sharing and on-demand streaming platform like YouTube capable of ingesting 500+ hours of uploaded video every minute and streaming billions of hours of low-latency adaptive video daily.
bullets: Functional: Resumable Large File Uploads: Creators upload raw video files up to 128 GB over potentially unstable connections with pause/resume support.

Functional: Parallel Multi-Resolution & Multi-Codec Transcoding: Convert raw uploads into multiple resolutions (`240p`, `360p`, `480p`, `720p`, `1080p`, `1440p`, `4K`) and codecs (`H.264/AVC`, `VP9`, `AV1`), generate thumbnail preview sprites, extract audio tracks, and produce HLS/DASH manifests.

Functional: Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) Playback: Viewers stream video with sub-second time-to-first-frame, dynamically switching video quality mid-stream based on client bandwidth and buffer occupancy without rebuffering.
Functional: Video Metadata & Engagement Counters: View video titles, descriptions, channels, and high-concurrency view/like counts.
Non-Functional: High Availability & Low Startup Latency: 99.99% playback availability; Time-to-First-Frame (TTFF) < 800ms globally; rebuffer ratio < 0.2%.

Non-Functional: Durability & Eventual Consistency: 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability on uploaded creator source files; eventual consistency is acceptable for view counts, likes, and newly published video search indexing.
Out of Scope: Ultra-low-latency WebRTC live streaming chat, recommendation ML collaborative filtering ranking models, and ContentID copyright lawsuit arbitration workflows.

sections.heading: 2. Traffic Modeling & Workload Assumptions
sections.body: We size the platform for YouTube-scale global traffic where egress bandwidth and storage dominate engineering costs.
bullets: Daily Active Users (DAU): 1 Billion DAU watching an average of 5 videos per day (average watched duration = 6 minutes per video).
Video Upload Rate: 500 hours of new video uploaded every minute = 720,000 hours of new video per day (~8.64 Million 5-minute videos uploaded/day).
Read:Write Ratio: ~580:1 video streams to uploads (5 Billion daily video views vs. 8.64 Million daily uploads).
Peak Traffic Multiplier: 2.5x global prime-time peak (8:00 PM–11:00 PM across major regional timezones).

Media Payload Sizes: Source upload bitrate ~15 Mbps (112 MB per minute). Transcoded ABR ladder total across 6 resolutions (H.264 + VP9/AV1) = ~25 Mbps combined (~187.5 MB per minute of video across all renditions). Average streamed bitrate per viewer (weighted around 720p/1080p VP9/AV1) = 3.5 Mbps.

sections.heading: 3. Back-of-the-Envelope Capacity Calculations
sections.body: Video streaming is the ultimate bandwidth and storage problem: a single 4-second 1080p segment is ~2 MB, so offloading 95%+ of traffic to ISP Edge CDNs is mandatory.
bullets: Upload & Playback QPS: 8.64M uploads/day / 86,400s = 100 Video Uploads/sec average (250 Peak). 5B video views/day / 86,400s = ~57,870 Playback Start QPS average (144,675 Peak). With 6-minute (360s) average watch time and 4-second HLS/DASH segments (90 segments/view), clients fetch 5B * 90 / 86,400s = **5.2 Million CDN segment requests/sec** average (**13 Million segment req/sec peak**).
Redis Metadata & View Counter Memory (RAM): 100 Million active/hot videos cached in Redis * 1 KB metadata + view/like Sharded Counter state = ~100 GB RAM across a regional Redis cluster.

5-Year Storage (Transcoded Video Corpus on S3/Colossus): 720,000 hours uploaded/day * 60 mins/hr = 43.2 Million minutes of new video/day. At ~187.5 MB/minute across the full multi-resolution ABR ladder = **8.1 PB/day** of new transcoded video! Over 5 years (1,825 days) = **~14.78 Exabytes (EB)** (using Reed-Solomon 10+4 erasure coding `1.4x` overhead instead of 3x replication saves ~23 EB of raw disks!).

Ingress & Egress Bandwidth: Upload Ingress = 500 hours/min = 30,000 seconds of video uploaded per real second * 15 Mbps (~1.875 MB/s) = **56.25 GB/s (450 Gbps)**. Playback Egress = 5 Billion views/day * 360s / 86,400s = ~20.83 Million concurrent active streams * 3.5 Mbps (0.4375 MB/s) = **9.11 TB/s (72.9 Tbps) average** -> **182 Tbps at 2.5x peak** served from global CDN Edge PoPs!

codeSnippet.code:
================================================================================
1. THROUGHPUT (QPS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Uploads per Day (5-min avg)            : 8,640,000 videos/day (500 hrs/min)
Upload Init QPS (Avg / Peak 2.5x)      : 100 QPS / 250 QPS
Upload Chunk PUT QPS (8MB chunks)      : ~7,000 chunk PUTs/sec avg

Daily Video Views                      : 5,000,000,000 views/day
Playback Manifest Start QPS (Avg/Peak) : 57,870 QPS / 144,675 QPS
4-Sec Segment Fetch QPS (CDN Edge)     : (5B * 90 segs) / 86,400 = 5,208,333 QPS
Peak CDN Segment Fetch QPS (2.5x)      : 13,020,833 QPS

================================================================================
2. METADATA & VIEW COUNTER MEMORY (REDIS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hot Video Metadata Cache (100M videos) : 100,000,000 * 1 KB = 100 GB RAM
Write-Behind Sharded View Counters     : 20M active videos * 256 B = 5.12 GB RAM
Total Redis Cluster Footprint          : ~128 GB per geographic region

================================================================================
3. 5-YEAR VIDEO STORAGE (MULTI-RESOLUTION ABR LADDER)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
New Video Minutes Uploaded / Day       : 720,000 hrs * 60 = 43,200,000 mins/day
Storage per Minute (240p..4K + Audio)  : ~187.5 MB / minute
Daily Transcoded Video Storage         : 43.2M * 187.5 MB = 8.10 PB / day
5-Year Raw Video Storage               : 8.10 PB * 365 * 5 = 14.78 Exabytes (EB)
With Reed-Solomon (10+4) Erasure Coding: 14.78 EB * 1.4 = 20.69 EB
  (Note: Cold videos with 0 views in 180 days discard intermediate VP9/AV1
   renditions and retain only H.264 + source, cutting cold storage by 60%!)

================================================================================
4. GLOBAL NETWORK BANDWIDTH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Upload Ingress (30,000 video-sec/s)    : 30,000 * 1.875 MB/s = 56.25 GB/s (450 Gbps)
Concurrent Active Viewers (Avg)        : (5B * 360s) / 86,400s = 20,833,333 viewers
Streaming Egress (Avg @ 3.5 Mbps)      : 20.83M * 3.5 Mbps = 72.9 Tbps (9.11 TB/s)
Streaming Egress (Peak 2.5x)           : 182.3 Tbps (96% offloaded at ISP CDN Edge)
================================================================================

sections.heading: 4. API Interface Contracts & Data Domain Models
sections.body: Core external REST/gRPC/WebSocket API contracts, request/response payloads, and underlying storage entities with primary keys (PK), foreign keys (FK), secondary/clustering indexes (IDX), and relationship cardinalities.
bullets: POST /api/v1/videos/uploads/init: Creates video metadata row in UPLOADING state and returns S3 Multipart Upload ID + Pre-Signed part URLs.
GET /api/v1/videos/{videoId}/playback: Returns HMAC-signed HLS (master.m3u8) and DASH (manifest.mpd) URLs routed to nearest ISP Edge PoP.
POST /api/v1/videos/{videoId}/heartbeat: Streams viewer watch-time progress and QoE rebuffering telemetry.

sections.heading: 5. High-Level Architecture Blueprint & Component Topology
sections.body: The architecture separates into three decoupled pipelines: (1) **Resumable Direct-to-Object-Store Upload**, (2) **DAG-Orchestrated Parallel GOP Transcoding**, and (3) **Hierarchical Multi-Tier Edge CDN ABR Delivery**.
bullets: Resumable Multipart Upload Gateway: Splits a 4 GB creator upload into 500 x 8 MB parts uploaded directly to S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoints. If the creator's Wi-Fi drops at 92%, the client queries completed part `ETag`s and resumes only the remaining 8%.

GOP Demuxer & DAG Transcoding Orchestrator: A 1-hour 4K video would take hours to transcode sequentially on one CPU. Instead, a fast Demuxer scans the video container headers (`moov` atom) and splits the video at **GOP (Group of Pictures / IDR Keyframe)** boundaries into 4-second chunks. It fans out `900 chunks x 6 resolutions` across thousands of spot GPU/ASIC workers in parallel, finishing a 1-hour video in under 60 seconds!

Two-Speed Encoding Strategy: Immediately encode `360p` and `720p` H.264 first so the video becomes playable (`status = READY`) within seconds of upload; asynchronously encode compute-heavy `1080p`/`4K` VP9 and AV1 renditions in the background.

Three-Tier CDN Hierarchy (ISP Edge -> Regional Shield -> S3 Origin): Immutable 4-second `.m4s` video segments are cached with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` at ISP PoPs, absorbing 96%+ of global egress.

sections.heading: 6. Deep-Dive Execution Flows & Core Logic
sections.body: We examine the two defining video pipelines: GOP-aligned parallel transcoding DAG execution on ingest and Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) HLS playback on stream delivery.
bullets: GOP-Aligned Parallel Transcoding DAG (Demuxer -> Transcoder Fleet): When an upload completes, the demuxer splits the raw video into 4-second Group-of-Pictures (GOP) segments aligned strictly at IDR keyframes. Segment encoding tasks are enqueued to Kafka, allowing a distributed fleet of GPU workers to transcode segments across multiple resolution profiles (`1080p`, `720p`, `480p`, `360p`) simultaneously in parallel.

Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) HLS Master Manifest (.m3u8) & CDN Streaming: When a user clicks play, the service validates access and returns a signed master `.m3u8` manifest containing variant streams (`1080p`, `720p`, `480p`, `360p`). The client video player dynamically samples download speed per 4-second segment and switches rendition bitrates seamlessly without buffering during network drops.

sections.heading: 7. Production Hardening, Fault Tolerance & Resilience
sections.body: At exabyte scale, optimizing encoding efficiency, hardware acceleration, and CDN cache hit ratios saves hundreds of millions of dollars per year.
bullets: Per-Title / Per-Scene Convex-Hull Encoding: A simple 2D cartoon or slide lecture looks crystal-clear at `1080p` using only `1.2 Mbps`, whereas a high-motion sports broadcast needs `6.5 Mbps`. Run a fast complexity probe pass on each GOP chunk to select the optimal `(resolution, CRF/bitrate)` points on the VMAF quality convex hull, cutting global bandwidth by 25–35%.

Custom Silicon Transcoding (Google Argos VCU / Hardware ASICs): Software CPU encoding of AV1 is 20x slower than H.264. Offload video transcoding to custom Video Coding Unit (VCU) ASICs, reserving expensive AV1/VP9 dual-pass encoding for videos that cross 1,000+ views/hour.

Popularity-Based Storage Tiering (Just-in-Time Transcoding for Cold Tail): Over 70% of uploaded videos receive fewer than 10 views per month. Delete bulky intermediate renditions (`1440p`, `480p`) for cold videos older than 90 days, keeping only the original archival master and `720p` H.264, and re-transcode on the fly if an old video suddenly goes viral.

Write-Behind Sharded View Counters + HyperLogLog Anti-Bot Filtering: A viral music video can receive 500,000 views/sec. Increment sharded counters in local Redis / Kafka streams (`view_count:{videoId}:{shard_0.63}`) and flush aggregated deltas to Vitess/MySQL every 30 seconds.

CMCD (Common Media Client Data) & Multi-CDN Traffic Steering: Players attach buffer health and throughput headers (`CMCD-Buffer`, `CMCD-Request`) on every `.m4s` fetch, while a real-time DNS/Manifest traffic router shifts viewers away from congested CDN PoPs across Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, and ISP OpenConnect boxes.

tradeOffs.option: HLS / MPEG-DASH over HTTP/3 (QUIC) with 4-Second fMP4 Segments
tradeOffs.pros: Works seamlessly with every global HTTP CDN cache, traverses corporate/mobile NAT firewalls effortlessly, and enables fine-grained ABR quality switching every 4 seconds.
tradeOffs.cons: Inherent 2–6 second latency floor compared to frame-by-frame WebRTC (irrelevant for on-demand VOD, mitigated via LL-HLS partial segments for live streams).
tradeOffs.bestFor: Global Video-on-Demand (VOD) platforms like YouTube, Netflix, and Disney+.

tradeOffs.pros: AV1 and VP9 reduce bitrate by 30–50% at identical perceptual quality (VMAF) compared to H.264, saving massive CDN egress costs.
tradeOffs.cons: Encoding AV1 requires 10x–15x more compute cycles than H.264, and older legacy TVs/IoT devices only have hardware decoders for H.264.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Tiered encoding: always encode H.264 for universal compatibility and fast-lane publishing; encode VP9/AV1 asynchronously for popular videos.

tradeOffs.option: Pre-Transcoding All Resolutions vs. Just-in-Time (On-the-Fly) Transcoding
tradeOffs.pros: Pre-transcoding guarantees zero compute latency at playback time and static CDN caching; Just-in-Time saves 70%+ storage on un-watched long-tail uploads.
tradeOffs.cons: Just-in-Time transcoding can overwhelm GPU pools if an uncached video suddenly goes viral.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Hybrid strategy: pre-transcode 360p/720p on upload, pre-transcode full 4K AV1 ladder for active channels, and evict intermediate renditions on cold archival videos.

interviewTip: In a YouTube interview, stand out by explaining **GOP-aligned parallel chunk transcoding** (splitting a raw video at IDR keyframes so 500 workers encode 4-second segments concurrently in under a minute) and **Two-Speed Encoding** (publishing 360p/720p H.264 immediately so the creator's video is playable in seconds, while queuing expensive 4K AV1 encoding asynchronously based on view velocity).
